name: XGBoost
summary: A regularised, highly optimised gradient-boosted tree library and algorithm for large tabular problems.
inputs: Tabular features (dense or sparse) and a target; optional sample weights.
outputs: Predictions or probabilities; SHAP-compatible tree structure.

data_requirements.frequency: Any; time-aware splits for time series

assumptions: Same as gradient boosting: tabular features, i.i.d. rows unless splits are time-aware
math_summary: Regularised gradient boosting: second-order (gradient and Hessian) approximation of the loss with L1/L2 penalties on leaf weights, plus a sparsity-aware split-finding algorithm and a weighted quantile sketch for approximate splits.
when_to_use: When you need a fast, mature boosted-tree library with GPU and distributed options
when_not_to_use: When a simpler model is needed for regulatory explainability
Raw sequences, images or text without features
pitfalls: Many hyperparameters: tune with time-aware CV
Feature importance (gain) can mislead; prefer SHAP or permutation importance

compute.complexity: Approximately O(n_trees * nnz * log n) with pre-sorted/hist methods; scales to billions of rows distributed.

applicability.use_case: Predicting next-period earnings surprises from fundamentals and filings metadata
Classifying commodity price regimes from macro drivers
